cards.front: Recall a key point about Thermoplastics and Thermosets
cards.back: Thermoplastics: linear polymer chains - soften when heated, solidify when cooled, can be remelted repeatedly. ABS (lego), acrylic (signs), PP (living hinges), HDPE (milk bottles).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Thermoplastics and Thermosets
cards.back: Thermosets: cross-linked polymer chains - set permanently once cured, cannot be remelted, char when reheated. Epoxy resin (adhesives), melamine (worktops), polyester resin (fibreglass).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Thermoplastics and Thermosets
cards.back: Polypropylene (PP): excellent fatigue resistance (living hinges on bottle caps), chemical resistant, lightweight, microwave-safe.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Thermoplastics and Thermosets
cards.back: Polycarbonate: virtually unbreakable, transparent, high impact resistance - safety glasses, riot shields, CDs.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Thermoplastics and Thermosets
cards.back: Recycling: thermoplastics are recyclable (melt and reform); thermosets cannot be melted down - ground into filler or burned for energy.

cards.front: What should you know about d&t exam tips?
cards.back: For polymer questions: 1) Classify as thermoplastic or thermoset, 2) Explain the chain structure, 3) State relevant properties, 4) Link to specific application, 5) Comment on recyclability if relevant.

Students often make mistakes here. Wrong: Thermosets are stronger than thermoplastics because they have cross-links, so they are always the better choice for strong products. Correct: Cross-links make thermosets rigid and heat-resistant but also brittle - they cannot absorb impact energy well.
